notes: Risk per trade: $150.00 (0.5% of $30,000.00; his band is 0.25-1%).

Cash-account planning reference: no leverage is assumed. The site does not read your broker's settled cash or buying power; confirm available settled cash before each buy.
Plan a protective stop-market order as soon as the buy fills; verify your broker supports the intended entry and linked stop orders. Gaps and slippage can make the loss exceed planned risk.

registry.coverage_note: A bounded manual registry of known cash-acquisition events, not a live news feed, exhaustive corporate-action screen, or clearance of unlisted stocks. _contract.schema_version: 2. The page refuses any other number rather than guessing at an older shape.
_contract.generated: When this file was written, ISO-8601 UTC. The page reads staleness off run.session, run.calendar and the browser's clock in ET; missing calendar evidence stays unknown.
_contract.app: Who wrote the file: the app name, its version, and rules_version -- a 12-hex digest of the rules block, so two nights under different constants never read as one screener.
_contract.cover: The night's verdict as sentences: h1, dek, the primary action's label and anchor, and the verb. Composed from the numbers below; never edited by hand.
_contract.run: The run that produced this file: session, session_state, expected_session, status (ok|degraded|closed|failed), problems (stage, kind, message -- kind is one of seven words and the page prints one fixed sentence per kind), versioned coverage ledger, universe snapshot provenance, input_basis (Alpaca daily feed, split adjustment and sessions), counts, email state, timings. run.sanitised counts the non-finite numbers replaced with null on the way in. run.timing is a different fact from the two above it: the session tonight's plans are FOR and the instants its entry window is scheduled between, offset and all. run.calendar records XNYS/library/version, measured/previous/next dates, actual open/close/shortened hours, completion buffer and a bounded browser schedule. Schedules may change. A record without it is one published before the field existed, and the page says entry timing is unavailable rather than guessing at a deadline. run.input_tolerance says whether a degraded acceptance is only the stale tail the recorded tolerance allows -- status ok beside acceptance degraded means exactly that -- and names those stocks; run.stale_followup reads the previous publication's stale stocks again from this run's fetch and never turns a late bar into a signal. run.reader_usage is what the night's chart reads cost in the API's own units -- calls sent, replies received, the four token classes -- under the model the run asked; it carries no price. run.intraday is the minute bars read for plans whose first day the daily bar could not place (a day that reached the trigger after the open): what tonight needed, asked for, fetched and stored under docs/intraday/, and the failures by kind; a plan walked from them names its object in minute_evidence. run.earnings is each published ticket's earnings warning, estimated from the company's SEC results filings (8-K item 2.02) a year back and read against the plan's hold window: an estimate and never an announced date, a warning and never a refusal, and a ticket SEC did not answer for says unknown; under version 2 each row also keeps the ticket's recent SEC current reports (8-K) and names the item codes they carry, a material item (1.01, 1.03, 2.01, 3.01, 5.01) by its heading and filing. run.sec_flags names each ticket's and listed setup's recent merger, tender-offer and deal filings by form and item code, a flag that holds the ticket for a person's review in orders.json and never a refusal or a clearance; run.cross_check reads each ticket's signal-day bar again from the iex feed, and a ticket whose two readings differ past the archived tolerances is blocked in orders.json.
_contract.nights: The last twenty runs as a ring: session, status, published_at. The reliability dots.
_contract.account: The configured sizing assumptions every plan below was computed from: equity, risk per trade, the position cap, the slot count. Not a balance, not settled cash, not buying power.
_contract.rules: Every strategy constant, keyed by module. Archived so the record says which screener made it.
_contract.breadth: The Market Monitor for the session and the regime verdict with its reasons verbatim. The size multiplier is the regime's; the plans already carry it.
_contract.bursts: Every 4% or $ breakout the scan found, graded, with its plan when it has one, its summary sentence and its series (last 120 bars, trades and the closest miss only). Scored or refused, a burst is here; a name that never burst is not. volume_vs_prior is the session's volume over the previous session's for every row, the $-only ones included (null when the previous session printed none); quality.burst holds the checklist's copy at two places.
_contract.trades: Tickers of the bursts to trade next session, ranked; those with order lines first. On a red regime this is empty whatever the grades say.
_contract.beyond_cap: Tickers of A-quality bursts with a plan and no ticket: withheld by the stop rule at the limit, past the slots or the configured equity, or sized to no whole share. Each has a reason in cash_budget.cut. Not checklist refusals.
_contract.cash_budget: Combined reaction and anticipation model allocation, reaction rank first: new tickets, principal reserved for unfinished model plans, model slots used, and every cut ticket with its setup kind and reason. Partial model sales do not free capacity. Never a balance, settled cash or buying power.
_contract.watchlist: Anticipation names: top (with a plan each) and also_quiet, with counts. Alerts, not trades.
_contract.open_plans: Every published plan still inside its window, replayed to this session as a model: status word, the instruction sentence, and for an uncertain fill the reason. SpicyStock does not know what you hold: a plan you never took is a row to ignore.
_contract.scorecard: All retained published plans in the stated window, including pending and missing evidence. Disjoint outcome counts reconcile to plans; rates use resolved plans alone, with an explicit denominator and minimum sample. Public model results, independent of personal selections.
_contract.closest_miss: On any night, the highest-scored burst not in trades and why it missed; the page shows it when trades is empty. Null when every burst is a trade or there were none.
_contract.scorecard_reading: The scorecard read honestly, beside its own numbers, which do not move: the model record's distinct setups, the model account each ticket was sized against, the stopped tickets at the session's close and low beside the stop they were booked at, the breadth figures this record computes differently from the publication before it, and where real trades are compared with the model (privately). Its sentences are printed verbatim.
_contract.candidate_checks: Each night's candidates read against SEC and a second price source, as flags for a reader: up to max_names names -- every ticket, every listed setup, every burst the review selected, every admitted burst in the trade band without a veto, then the also-quiet coils -- each with its recent merger, tender and deal filings, its earnings estimate from SEC results filings and its recent 8-K items, and its signal-day bar read again from the iex feed. A name past the bound is counted by role. A name the tickets' own blocks read carries their reading. It changes no plan, ticket or order, unknown is never clear, and its sentence is printed verbatim.
_contract.funnel: Where every discovered reaction candidate and every listed anticipation setup stopped: one terminal stage each, in the order the run applies its gates, so the stage counts sum to the discovered count. Derived from the fields above and re-derived by the validator; the labels the page and the mail print travel with it. A stage is the record's own accounting of its gates, never a judgement of the setup and never an entry.
_contract.observations: Public coverage of every published saveable signal, independent of local saves. Each signal keeps its own identity and 21-calendar-day window. Symbols carry the latest real bar plus up to 20 dated observations from already-fetched frames; missing bars stay missing, and missing frames retain earlier actual observations. This is research coverage, never a quote feed or personal trading history.
_contract._contract: This paragraph per key. If a key is here and not above, or above and not here, the file is refused.
